scenes.title: What is Workflow Orchestration?
scenes.narration: This lesson defines workflow orchestration and explains why data teams need it once pipelines grow beyond a single script.

scenes.title: The problem with cron
bullets: Cron runs scripts blindly at fixed times
No awareness of dependencies between jobs
No retries, alerting, or visibility on failure
scenes.narration: Many teams start by scheduling scripts with cron, but cron simply fires a command at a fixed time with no understanding of what else is happening. It has no concept of one job depending on another, so a downstream step can run on stale data. And when something fails, cron offers no automatic retries, no alerting, and no visibility into what went wrong.

scenes.title: What an orchestrator adds
bullets: A UI for monitoring, logs, and reruns
scenes.narration: A workflow orchestrator fixes exactly these gaps. It runs tasks in dependency order so a step only starts once its inputs are ready, it retries transient failures and alerts you when something truly breaks, and it provides a user interface where you can watch runs, read logs, and rerun failed pieces without touching the command line.

scenes.title: Anatomy of a pipeline
scenes.narration: A typical orchestrated pipeline chains several distinct stages. First raw data is ingested, then it is transformed with tools like dbt or Spark, then quality tests validate the results, and finally the data is published to business intelligence tools with alerts on completion. The orchestrator's job is to guarantee these stages run in the right order and to react intelligently when any of them fails.

scenes.title: The main tools
scenes.narration: Three tools dominate this space. Airflow is the mature industry standard, modeling pipelines as task-centric DAGs written in Python with an enormous ecosystem. Dagster and Prefect are newer challengers that rethink the model, with Dagster centering on data assets and Prefect on flexible Python flows, both emphasizing easier local testing and cleaner developer ergonomics.

scenes.text: Orchestration is about running the right tasks in the right order with retries, alerting, and visibility, so pipelines stay reliable as they grow.
scenes.narration: The core idea to carry forward is that orchestration means running the right tasks in the right order with built-in retries, alerting, and visibility, which is what keeps data pipelines reliable as they grow in size and complexity.
